observations.text: SP, due to insufficient study of the daily assignment, did not know in detail the formation exercises briefed for the sortie and could not state the applicable BD 3-1/HATC handbook references. The pre-flight briefing was completed only after the IP directed the content and presented part of the material. Further study of the assigned exercises is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, could not explain the formation break-up sequence from the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual when questioned at the pre-flight briefing. The item was resolved only when the IP provided the procedure and worked it through with the SP. Review of the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual before the next formation sortie is required.

SP knew the exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual with confidence at the pre-flight briefing, within the standards for this block. Two references to the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 formation paragraphs were stated correctly only after the IP's verbal prompts, and were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recall of the published references is expected to improve.

SP knew in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and answered questions on formation positions and visual signals from the Flight Manual without IP prompting. Minor gaps on the meteorological material of the morning briefing were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP presented the daily assignment accurately and rapidly and used the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual and the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 with confidence at both briefings, without IP prompting. Questions on airport traffic procedures and on the flight planning of the formation recovery were answered completely and without hesitation. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated knowledge well above the level required for this block, explaining theoretically the aerodynamic effects of the position changes flown and relating them to the formation profile. Every handbook required by BD 3-1/HATC, together with the aeronautical publications, was used with confidence and without a single reference error at the pre-flight and post-flight briefings. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to preparation limited to the material of the previous sortie, did not know the exercises given as daily assignment and could not state the briefed join-up and rejoin procedures at the pre-flight briefing. The briefing was completed only because the IP directed the sequence and presented part of the material. Further study of the assigned exercises is required.

SP, due to planning conducted without the current publication for the route, could not extract the formation recovery information required from the MAIP and the en route maps. The planning was produced only after the IP located the publications and worked the sequence with the SP. Use of current aeronautical publications during mission planning is required.

SP, due to fragmented study of the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual, did not state the lost wingman procedure in the prescribed sequence at the pre-flight briefing, omitting two steps. The sequence was completed correctly only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the omissions were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to incomplete knowledge of the limits applicable to the maneuver, did not state the published airspeed and bank restrictions for the formation rejoin when questioned during the flight. The correct limits were given only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the item was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP knew the exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual and the aeronautical publications correctly at both briefings, within the standards for this block. Minor gaps on meteorological principles were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, but recurred on the same subject at the post-flight briefing. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consolidation of the meteorological material is expected to improve.

SP knew in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and used all handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC with confidence, answering questions on formation procedures accurately and rapidly. Airport traffic procedures and the flight planning of the formation recovery were presented completely and without IP prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional depth of knowledge, explaining theoretically the aerodynamic causes of the closure observed during the rejoin and relating them to the published Flight Manual data. Questions on flight physiology under sustained G and on sea and land survival procedures with SAR means were answered in full and without hesitation at the post-flight briefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient study of the material assigned for the sortie, did not know in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and could not state the briefed formation maneuvers or their sequence. The pre-flight briefing was completed only after the IP directed the presentation and executed part of it. Further study of the assigned exercises before the next formation sortie is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, could not state the lost wingman actions for the formation when questioned in flight. The IP had to provide the procedure and direct its application, with the result that the exercise continued only under IP direction. Review of the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to study limited to the Flight Manual alone, did not use the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 formation paragraphs when asked to justify the briefed separation and lighting requirements. The correct references were produced only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the omission was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to mission planning that did not address the forecast weather at the recovery time, did not present the meteorological picture for the formation recovery at the pre-flight briefing. The material was covered only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the alternates for the formation were identified with delay.

SP, due to compressed preparation of the aeronautical publications, quoted the wrong MAIP reference for the formation recovery route at the pre-flight briefing. The error was recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and the remainder of the planning was presented correctly.

SP, due to lack of awareness of a published restriction that was available in the briefing material, stated the altitude block for the formation join-up incorrectly during the pre-flight briefing. The error was recognized and corrected by the SP from the Flight Manual in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP knew in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual and the aeronautical publications with confidence at both briefings, within the standards for this block. Answers on air medicine and flight physiology were correct but slow, and one item on sea and land survival with SAR means required a second attempt before it was complete. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed and confidence in the non-flying subject areas are expected to improve.

SP demonstrated knowledge well above the required level, using with confidence every handbook required by BD 3-1/HATC and explaining theoretically the aerodynamic effects encountered in the positions flown during the sortie. Questions on airport traffic procedures, meteorological principles and sea and land survival with SAR means were answered in full, accurately and rapidly, at both briefings, and no knowledge deviation was identified. Above end of block MIF achieved.
